chosen_configuration.snr_mask: off for rover and base; all frequency masks zero

decision_policy: The 7 degree elevation mask is a predeclared scientific configuration choice. All other configuration was selected from frozen preprocessing semantics, observed system support, historical configuration, and official RTKLIB source semantics; no Ibiza ground-truth accuracy was used and the mask must not be tuned further using ground truth.

previous_local_rtklib_configuration_obse.source_status: pre-existing local untracked configuration; intentionally deleted before the controlled experiment

settings_observed_before_deletion.troposphere: est-ztd (handled as Saastamoinen by official pntpos.c)

material_semantic_mismatches: The predeclared 7 degree RTKLIB elevation mask differs from TASGNSS, which has no TASGNSS-level elevation mask and retains observations below 7 degrees.
RTKLIB applies its conventional elevation/system-dependent stochastic model and chi-square/GDOP validation; neutral TASGNSS uses an identity weight matrix and its own iterative solver acceptance.
RTKLIB and TASGNSS have different state layouts, iteration paths, code-bias handling details, and initialization/reuse behavior; these are intrinsic solver differences, not tuned away.

The RTKLIB SPP configuration consumes the first-frequency code according to RTKLIB signal-priority rules; this is technically close to, but not an exact semantic identity with, TASGNSS's first populated pseudorange slot.
No RTKLIB setting reproduces the TDL feature-validity filter. That filter is used only to declare the frozen 2,849 comparison timestamps after full-interval RTKLIB solving.
